newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banks mulling possibility of mergers - banker.
newsitem.headline: German banks mulling possibility of mergers - banker.

text.p: Most bankers in Germany have considered the possibility that merger activity may break out in their sector, the chief executive of Germany's fifth-largest bank said on Thursday.
"Every banker has thought over all possibilities," Eberhard Martini, chief executive of Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel- Bank AG, or Hypo-Bank, told a news conference.
"It could well be that the current market speculation about mergers will blow over. But we as managers must be prepared for all eventualities."
Martini added that his bank was confident it would be able to remain independent.

But bank mergers in other countries, coupled with the announcement by Deutsche Bank AG in July that it had amassed a 5.21 percent stake in Bayerische Vereinsbank, had set off a wave of merger speculation, Martini said.
"If the market changes, which we do not expect at present, we will take an active role in shaping events in the interests of our customers, staff and shareholders."
"We would be stupid if we just sat there like rabbits in front of a snake, we want to take an active role."

Martini's comments come amid heavy gains in German bank shares this week, led by Commerzbank AG, which some share dealers have attributed to a fresh upsurge in rumours of mergers and takeovers in Germany's overcrowded banking market.

His remarks are more frank than comments made by the heads of Germany's other top five banks who have recently all but dismissed the possibility of mergers and said that the publicly-owned banks were more in need of consolidation than the private ones.
Martini noted that the merger of Chemical Banking Corp and Chase Manhattan in the U.S. earlier this year was initiated by a fund manager who persuaded other fund managers to agree to the idea.
"The banks' management had no option but to accept the facts," Martini said.
Merged Dutch bank ABN-Amro, by contrast, resulted from the respective management boards deciding to gain synergy benefits, Martini said.
He noted that both bank mergers appeared to have been successful.
Martini noted that Hypo-Bank's own share price had surged 30 percent since Deutsche's stake announcement in July.

Hypo-Bank itself has been mooted as a possible merger partner for Dresdner Bank AG because insurance giant Allianz AG Holding holds stakes of more than 20 percent in each of them and may instigate a tie-up.
